text:
# Face Culling and Visibility Optimization

Also called: Interior Polygon Removal, Removing Interior Polygons

## Overview
Face Culling and Visibility Optimization reduces the rendering load of blocky voxel meshes by reconstructing cubes from triangles and removing sides that are adjacent to solid neighbors, thereby avoiding the rendering of 12 triangles (6 sides) when only 2 triangles (1 side) are visible [S1, unofficial]. It differs from its siblings by focusing on the immediate geometric adjacency of voxels to eliminate internal faces, whereas methods like [Block Visibility Culling](5334-block-visibility-culling.md) operate on camera-relative orientation and [Opacity-based Mesh Culling](8759-opacity-based-mesh-culling.md) rely on material transparency properties.

## Shared principles
The core mechanism involves iterating through occupied voxel positions and evaluating the six potential faces (normals $\pm x, \pm y, \pm z$) of each voxel. For each face, the algorithm checks the state of the immediate neighbor in the direction of the face normal. If the neighbor is solid (non-empty), the face is considered internal and is culled; otherwise, it is exposed and added to the mesh buffer. This logic assumes a [uniform grid](#920-uniform-grid.md) where voxel centers are integer coordinates and neighbors are at distance 1.

## Subtopics

### [Voxel Block Placement with Face Culling](923-voxel-block-placement-with-face-culling.md)
A technique for dynamically updating a voxel chunk's internal state and face visibility when blocks are placed or removed, using neighbor checks to toggle shared faces without regenerating the entire mesh. It differs from its sibling [Greedy face merging](8935-greedy-face-merging.md) by maintaining per-block visibility flags rather than merging adjacent quads into larger primitives, and from [Blocky meshing](31-blocky-meshing.md) generally by focusing on incremental state updates rather than batch mesh generation.

### [Voxel Block Shape & Culling Configuration](2176-voxel-block-shape-culling-configuration.md)
A trait-based system that defines the geometry, transparency culling behavior, and lighting properties for individual block types in a voxel mesh generator. It solves the problem of hard-coded block logic by decoupling block identity from mesh generation, allowing different block types to specify their own shape (e.g., cube, ramp, fluid) and culling mode (e.g., opaque, transparent merged). It sets itself apart from sibling methods by providing a per-block configuration interface rather than a global culling rule or a post-generation optimization pass.

### [Face Coverage Mask Culling](3397-face-coverage-mask-culling.md)
A method for optimizing blocky mesh generation by representing the geometric coverage of a voxel face as a bit mask, allowing for the culling of partially occluded faces from partial shapes (such as stairs and slabs). Unlike basic neighbor checks that treat faces as binary solid/empty, this method solves the problem where a boolean solid flag is insufficient because partial shapes have mixed visible and hidden areas on a single face. It sets itself apart from [Face Culling](8735-face-culling.md) by enabling fine-grained visibility decisions based on geometric overlap rather than simple adjacency, and from [Opacity-based Mesh Culling](8759-opacity-based-mesh-culling.md) by separating geometric coverage from material transparency properties.

### [ChunkMesh Vertex Packing and Management](3566-chunkmesh-vertex-packing-and-management.md)
A dynamic mesh generation and buffer management technique for voxel terrain that packs vertex attributes into compact 32-bit integers and manages incremental updates via a free-list of reusable vertex indices. It solves the problem of high memory overhead and frequent GPU buffer uploads in [blocky meshing](#31-blocky-meshing.md) by reducing vertex data size and avoiding reallocation. It differs from [Voxel Face Meshing with Packed Attributes](4153-voxel-face-meshing-with-packed-attributes.md) by managing the host-side buffer state and reuse logic, whereas the sibling focuses on the shader-side unpacking layout; it differs from [Mesh Reindexing and Vertex Compaction](4160-mesh-reindexing-and-vertex-compaction.md) by reusing indices in place rather than compacting the array [G].

### [Voxel Backface Culling and Internal Face Masking](4569-voxel-backface-culling-and-internal-face-masking.md)
A visibility [optimization technique](#7922-optimization-technique.md) for blocky meshing that rejects invisible faces by determining front/back orientation in projection space and masking faces shared between neighboring voxels. It differs from sibling methods like [Face Coverage Mask Culling](3397-face-coverage-mask-culling.md) by operating directly on the [geometry shader](#4369-geometry-shader-quads.md) stage using projection-space dot products rather than pre-computed coverage masks, and from [Opacity-based Mesh Culling](8759-opacity-based-mesh-culling.md) by relying on geometric occlusion (internal faces) rather than alpha thresholds.

### [Block Visibility Culling](5334-block-visibility-culling.md)
Determines which voxel blocks require mesh updates or rendering based on the camera's position and rotation, avoiding unnecessary geometry generation when the viewing direction or position has not changed significantly. It operates at the coarse block level by comparing current camera coordinates against previous frame values to skip index updates entirely, or by calculating screen-space projections to cull invisible faces based on surface orientation relative to the player. Unlike [Voxel Face Visibility Check](6723-voxel-face-visibility-check.md), which evaluates individual faces within a block, this method makes decisions about entire blocks or large face groups based on camera movement.

### [Extraction of Surface Points (Sobierajski)](5721-extraction-of-surface-points-sobierajski.md)
A fast display method for the direct rendering of boundary surfaces by extracting only visible boundary voxels from volume data. It solves the problem of rendering speed in volume visualization by avoiding the processing of occluded geometry. Unlike sibling methods that operate on blocky meshes or cull faces after mesh generation, this method operates at the voxel level, projecting surface points directly to the image plane. It sets itself apart by using a multi-view visibility test to pre-filter voxels and projecting each voxel to multiple pixels to prevent image holes, rather than relying on polygon rasterization.

### [Mask Projection Culling](6836-mask-projection-culling.md)
A visibility-based mesh filtering technique that removes faces and vertices not consistently observed across multiple camera poses by projecting points into camera space and comparing their depth against rendered depth maps or binary masks. It differs from sibling methods like [Face Coverage Mask Culling](3397-face-coverage-mask-culling.md) by relying on explicit depth comparison and multi-view consistency rather than simple 2D coverage, and from [Block Visibility Culling](5334-block-visibility-culling.md) by operating on individual mesh primitives rather than volumetric blocks. It is particularly useful for cleaning up noisy reconstructions from [NeRF](#1185-nerf-neural-radiance-fields.md) or [Gaussian Splatting](#946-gaussian-splatting.md) pipelines where geometry may extend into empty space or background regions.

### [Mesh Culling via 3D Projection and Connected Components](6963-mesh-culling-via-3d-projection-and-connected-components.md)
This method removes geometric artifacts and occluded regions from a 3D mesh by projecting its vertices into multiple camera views and comparing their depths against reference depth maps. It classifies mesh faces as "seen" (visible in at least 20 views), "unseen," or "forecast" (distant but potentially valid) to filter out noise from unbounded reconstructions. Unlike sibling methods that rely on voxel adjacency or backface normals, this approach uses multi-view consistency to determine visibility, making it suitable for cleaning meshes derived from Gaussian Splatting or similar radiance field representations.

### [Face Culling](8735-face-culling.md)
A mesh generation optimization that reduces the number of vertices sent to the GPU by skipping the rendering of voxel faces that are adjacent to existing neighboring voxels. It solves the problem of naively rendering all 6 faces of every cube, including those hidden by neighbors. It is distinguished from its siblings by its direct, per-voxel neighbor lookup logic applied during mesh creation, rather than post-generation filtering or complex visibility preprocessing.

### [Opacity-based Mesh Culling](8759-opacity-based-mesh-culling.md)
Removes geometric primitives from a polygonal mesh representation of a scene based on their accumulated opacity values, retaining only those faces that contribute significantly to the visual output. This method addresses the problem of excessive mesh complexity and storage overhead in [neural radiance field (NeRF)](#834-neural-radiance-field-nerf.md) extractions by discarding transparent or low-opacity triangles. It differs from its siblings, such as [Face Culling](8735-face-culling.md) which relies on voxel adjacency, and [Block Visibility Culling](5334-block-visibility-culling.md) which operates on larger chunks, by evaluating the intrinsic opacity of individual mesh faces or triangles rather than their spatial neighbors.

### [From-Region Visibility Preprocessing](9048-from-region-visibility-preprocessing.md)
[From-region visibility preprocessing](#9048-from-region-visibility-preprocessing.md) is a technique that precomputes which parts of a 3D scene are visible from specific regions of the camera space, allowing the renderer to skip occluded geometry. It differs from standard occlusion culling by shifting the heavy computation to an offline phase, enabling real-time rendering with strict accuracy guarantees, albeit at the cost of significant preprocessing time.

### Buried Bitmask Optimization
A bitmask used to track which blocks in a chunk are 'buried' (fully surrounded by opaque blocks), allowing the renderer to skip mesh generation for those blocks [S2, unofficial]. The algorithm resets the buried bitmask for the chunk, creates `MappedAdjacentChunks` for the current chunk position to access neighboring chunks, and iterates through all blocks in the chunk (0 to `CHUNK_SIZE`). For each block, it determines if it is buried by calling `block->isBuried(...)` and sets the corresponding flag in the bitmask. If all blocks in the chunk are buried (checked via `buriedBitmask->AreAllBlocksSet()`), the mesh is marked as empty and mesh generation is skipped. When generating the mesh, any block that is air or has its buried flag set in the bitmask is skipped [S2, unofficial].

### Two-pass transparent meshing with opaque separation
A meshing strategy that separates opaque and transparent geometry into two passes to ensure correct rendering order and reduce overdraw, by generating opaque faces between air/transparent blocks and transparent faces only for blocks touching air [S3, unofficial]. The algorithm first checks if the chunk contains any transparent blocks; if not, the second pass is skipped. In the first (opaque) pass, if the chunk contains transparent blocks, it tests for opaque blocks (ignoring transparent and air) to generate opaque faces between air and transparent blocks; otherwise, it tests for non-air blocks. In the second (transparent) pass, it tests for non-air blocks to mark only transparent blocks, generating faces for all transparent blocks touching air but not adding faces between transparent and solid blocks (since solid blocks already have those faces). To prevent solid faces from being added in the transparent pass, the algorithm checks if it is in the transparent pass before constructing the AO value and adding the block type to the hashmap, ignoring any block types that are not transparent [S3, unofficial].

### Smart Leaf Rendering
A leaf block rendering strategy that preserves alpha cutouts on outer leaf surfaces while culling internal faces to reduce vertex count [S4, unofficial]. The behavior is controlled by a global static enum `sLeafRenderMode`, which defaults to `ChunkRenderer::LeafRenderMode::Smart` [S4, unofficial].

### Hidden Face Extension
A proposed optimization where the 2D grid includes a 'don't care' state (2) to allow rectangles to extend into hidden areas, potentially reducing total rectangle count [S5, unofficial]. While this might reduce mesh size, it increases the load on the rasterizer [S5, unofficial].

## Background
The concept of removing interior polygons to improve rendering performance originated in early voxel engine implementations, such as those for Minecraft-like [games](#12542-games-gaussian-mesh-splatting.md). The initial brute-force approach instantiated models of cubes, leading to unnecessary rendering of internal triangles. To optimize this, a class was added to reconstruct cubes from triangles and check for solid neighbors, determining which sides to render. If a neighbor existed, the adjacent side was not rendered. To further optimize, the meshes of all cubes were combined into a single big mesh called a 'chunk' [S1, unofficial]. This approach addressed the limitation of rendering engines (like Unity) which restrict mesh vertex counts, by allowing chunks to be stacked or managed efficiently [S1, unofficial].
